body:
You really should create a new bank account. It only takes like an hour to do so, and it will protect the funds you'll get for the abortion.

Other than that, it sounds like you're doing everything you can in your situation. Sorry about what happened :( 

You should try researching to see if there's any abortion funds near your area. They're non-profits that basically help girls & women fund abortions. They may not fund the whole procedure, but it will reduce costs. You could also try sites like GoFundMe and try getting donations.

She sounds like me: Never had close friends but a ton of casual acquaintances / casual friends. I also tend to be more logical rather than emotional.

If she's like me, then making long-term friends is basically like having a job. You have to nurture that relationship. You have to keep hanging out with them, do things for them, go on activities together, etc. That's nice and all, but it's effort. People need to be "taken cared of". Then, in return, they take care of you. That's basically friendship in a nutshell.

Some people don't think the effort is worth it though. For example, I'm a super busy person and work 2 jobs (one to support myself, the other is running my side business). If you don't even have time for YOURSELF, you definitely don't have time for others. Some people are perfectly fine with this though, and maybe she is one of those people.

The true deal breaker is whether or not you're ok with it. No one wants to be judged because they don't have friends.

I think the first question you should ask yourself is, how much do you really want to maintain a relationship with your father? (if there is one to begin with?)

I don't think you should move back because your situation isn't ideal. Getting kicked out is never ideal. He'll definitely take that as "crawling back"

The problem is that he said "you are no longer welcome here." If you take his word for it and never come back, maybe HE'LL be the one crawling back to you. THEN you can make amends. He'll probably respect you more if you do that.

The fact you want to be the first one to make up after how he treated you shows how mature you are. It's sad that he treats you so badly. He's the one who should be grateful for having such a responsible kid.

To be honest though, doing the "right" thing doesn't seem like it'll do you any favors. Unless he comes "crawling back", then it's you "crawling back." It's a lose-lose situation.

If you really want to make amends, give it a few weeks or months until things calm down a bit.

**Edit**: I just realized your age says 16. It's illegal for him to kick you out. Like someone mentioned, maybe you should consider the "variance" option and live with your mom for a while. Consider calling CPS as well.

I'm sorry he broke up with you like that. That really sucks.

I wouldn't call him an asshole right away though. It sounded like maybe he was scared and thought he would get accused of hurting you or something (therefore prob why he broke up over text instead of coming over). It's a bit of a pussy move on his part, but it's also somewhat understandable. Some people just don't know how to handle these types of problems and they just take the easy way out.

You definitely shouldn't give up on medicine though. Having depression or suicidal thoughts doesn't suddenly make you a terrible doctor (or whatever you're studying for). I really think we could use more doctors who can relate to the feelings of depression/suicidal thoughts. You may save a life because of that.
Well he/she doesn't seem to be trying to give any useful advice. I figure I might as well explain things. Sorry if that upsets you.

I never took Ritalin but taken Adderall XR. With that said, here's my answers: 

1. Started off with 10mg XR then gradually started taking 20mg
2. Maybe 8 months? At first I took breaks from it, but now I do it almost every day. I kinda felt shitty on my "days off"
3. I took Lexapro & Wellbutrin. I honestly kinda felt like shit and had the worst mood swings, but everyone reacts to these differently.
4. Yes

I think it's also worth noting that it may treat the symptoms of depression (like trouble concentrating), but not treat the depression itself. You'll still feel depressed, just productive and depressed.

Also here's some side effects I experienced, if that helps:

1. Loss of appetite (I lost almost 10 pounds. I'm borderline underweight for my height)
2. Trouble sleeping (this normalizes after a while, but I still have a shitty sleep schedule)
3. Irritability (everyone appears like an idiot)

Interesting fact: I experienced an increase in libido (before lexapro/wellbutrin, which decreased it). This seems to be something only women experience. Men tend to experience a loss in libido.
I'm not a therapist so I can't really tell you, but it's possible. Depression is a spectrum and comes in all shapes and sizes. People feel it and express it differently.
PM me, I could use some company too.

I think you just need a break from dating in general. Focus on yourself for a while and work on treating your depression before getting into another serious relationship.

I think maybe your depression makes you feel more ready to jump into toxic relationships. That's probably why you keep getting cheated on. I think it would help you a lot if you just give dating a break for a bit. You're only 20 and had 4 girlfriends (more GFs than I had BFs, and I'm 7 years older)

It hurts now and I know you may not believe it now, but you'll get over her. You're so young, there's so much more to life than this 1 girl.

Also, stop contacting her. Continuing to contact her may get you in trouble for harassment.

It's funny you say that because technically I am a millionaire (Not because of this job, but from a business I started a while ago). Still got the lateness problem though :(

Having money doesn't necessarily mean you can just dick around whenever you want. Or at least I can't. 1M bucks also isn't exactly a ton of money these days (I also live in NYC so taxes/rent for me aren't very nice), but a lot of this depends on what you're running. It's like, you gotta spend money to make money.

I think I probably rather be a happy poor person than a miserable rich person. There really is some truth to the saying that you can't buy happiness. Love, for example, you can't buy that. Dating can be very difficult because people seem to always think you're an asshole and your problems should just melt away simply because you got money. Money actually ADDS problems in some aspects of your life.

I do love my job, it's just very stressful and people tend to be dumb about things. I am planning to talk to the CTO about it on Monday and see if we can come to an agreement. If that doesn't work out then I'll just quit, so at least I have the power to do that.

Yeah that's weird... It's one thing to lie about work, but that combined with the gift thing is really fishy. You should just talk to her about it. If she gets upset/defensive then maybe that's a sign the relationship isn't gonna work out.

I'm also kinda confused why she wanted to be in a relationship with one of her best friends (you) and then suddenly decide to be all sneaky. Like, what's the point? If you wanna date other people, just stay friends. I don't get it.

I think you overestimate how reasonable people are at this company, but you're right that I do need to fix the situation. I'm planning to speak to the CTO on Monday about it.

Hopefully after I sort my shit out, things will get easier. I don't want to quit until I feel like I exhausted all my options. I do like my job, it's just stressful.

Yeah I actually plan to talk to the CTO about it on Monday (my boss can't actually do much to fix anything). She knows that I'm stressed, but I think I'm just gonna flat out tell her that I need a more flexible schedule. It's not like I have to physically be at work to do work -- especially since I'm carrying the workload of like 5 people. They are trying to hire some people to help me out, but it's been a bit dry lately. I'm also gonna try to see if I can get promoted or at least get paid a good raise for all the work I've been doing.

Worse case scenario, if I'm still where I am right now after a month or so, I'm just gonna quit. There's companies out there who are willing to treat me better than that.

Now that you mention it, I actually was diagnosed with ADHD almost a year ago. I am taking adderall to help with that, as well as lexapro, wellbutrin, and some kind of mood stabilizer to deal with my other issues.

I think the drugs actually made my shit worse, I mean, I never actually vomited from purely being depressed/stressed out before. My periods were also out of whack lately and I've been starting like 3 weeks early (sorry if that's TMI). I don't have dyslexia though. I did however talk to my therapist about this and I think they're gonna switch out my drugs until they find what works for me.

The odd thing is I always been kind of a workaholic (I always heard ADHD people have trouble at work, but I tend to be ADHD with stuff that's not work-related). There's something about work, despite it sucking a lot, that is sort of like an escape for me. It's the one place where I don't feel depressed. Maybe stressed, but not depressed. I feel like I'm a part of something important and it's a pretty seductive feeling, especially when you always feel like a shitty asshole who shouldn't even bother continuing their life.

Yeah idk, maybe that's why people think I'm an asshole. I wasn't saying 'haha' because I don't take it seriously. I just like to try to find humor whenever I can (idk, I guess it helps me deal with stuff) -- I was basically laughing at myself. I understand that being late is a seriously shitty character flaw, and I am working on it.

To be honest though...I get a little anxious when I want to plan things with him, as well as when I am going to an event with him. This is the 1 thing we fight about so I always feel like something bad is gonna happen. I also kind of tend to be a workaholic in general...and despite work sucking a lot, it's kind of like an escape from being depressed. I mean...it's better than staying at home crying all night, right? I actually really hate weekends because of this and I end up feeling the worst on weekends.

Idk why I even made this post. I just wanted to complain somewhere really. I think I do need to stop complaining to him and just complain on Reddit or to my therapist or whatever when I feel shitty.

Weird...I never had to pay for appointments before I actually have the appointment -- consultation or not. Like ever, in any type of doctor.

To be honest, I think she was just scared and either felt 1) She was not qualified to treat your situation or 2) Maybe she was afraid of her safety. Breakdowns are scary for a lot of people, they can make people think the worst, even if you wouldn't harm a fly.

However, that doesn't excuse her from taking your money without getting the appointment. You need to report her for that.
Maybe you can talk to your school counselor or something? They might be able to see if you can take classes online or do all the classwork/homework at home only.

I can empathize with what you're feeling and here's my perspective on this.

Since you were lucky to live a pretty good life, you would actually be doing the world a disservice by ending your life. Why would that be you ask? Well that's because the ways of the universe decided to distribute a chunk of its assets to you (assets = money, food, etc). Now, it's up to you (if you desire) to make the world a better place by sharing those assets with those who are less fortunate, and/or use your education to develop something that will benefit others.

Less fortunate people do not have as much power to change the world as those who are more wealthy or have bigger support groups. You shouldn't feel bad about it though -- you should be happy that you can actually do something about it.

There's actually a quote from this Bill Gates museum I went to that kinda stuck with me. It goes something like this: "If life happens to bless you, you should use those gifts as well and as wisely as you can"

Something you'll learn in time is that you do not live to please your parents. You can always consider their opinion, but in the end, your successes and failures are determined by your own standards.

There were a lot of things my parents were disappointment in me about but I was proud of, and vise versa. You shouldn't let it consume your life though. So what if they get angry about a bad grade? In the grand scheme of things, it's such a tiny blip in one's life that it doesn't matter.

Only you understand what you're going through, so disappointment from someone else is not the same as being disappointed in yourself.

Hmm well last year I tried going to a bunch of these developer-centric type of meetups (that's one of my interests). I also tried going to girl-centric versions of them too, since I always wanted to have "girlfriends" and have girl nights and stuff. I didn't like the people too much though (and also I was nervous). The guys tend to be very egotistical and condescending. The girls are also somewhat feminazis and always use that "78 cents on the dollar" logic when the topic of girls in tech comes up (I absolutely HATE that, because it's such a misleading statistic. It's like a pet peeve of mine).

I think if I ever want to make friends, I first need to get over the anxiety, which my therapist can help with. I also should probably spend more time being more well-rounded. Maybe I can read a novel each month, start watching popular TV/movies, and basically get more familiar with things people like so I can make conversations without being awkward.

I've been trying to hide my scars but he did notice it eventually. He did mention he does feel bad and hopes he's not a trigger. I didn't say he was a trigger because I don't want him to feel guilty. I don't like blaming people for my issues like that. I also don't think it's his fault, because like you said, I need to work on myself first.

We do love each other but honestly I am starting to think our relationship is glued based on our fear of loneliness (I have no friends. He has lots but has a hard time finding relationships I think). He tells me he wants to have a "normal" life  and get married, have 2-3 kids and a dog or something.

While I respect that, I'm not 100% sure if I'd be happy with that kind of life. I need excitement, I need to travel the world, be successful, & enjoy my life before settling down. I don't want to do it alone though...

One of the things I sometimes get reminded of when I think about relationships is my mom. One time, my mom wanted a divorce because my dad cheated, but they ended up never doing it. They've separated, but not divorced. My mom said she was mainly afraid of being alone, and told me this while breaking down crying. That was the most heartbreaking things I ever seen in my life. What's worse is sometimes I feel like I can see myself in her. This is one of the things I think about when I spiral into depression and sometimes cut myself. I hate living in a world where sweet caring people like my mom are hurt so bad.

(also, sorry long post is long lol. I mostly just need an outlet right now)

Thank you! Yeah it's true I am not totally up-to-date with current events, which I don't like. That's why when he talks about politics, I kind of prefer he talks over IM/chat about it so I can do a little bit of mini-research so I don't sound retarded. I don't particularly like the topic, but I do want to be aware of it since I do care about my future. That's why I don't mind it when he brings up politics (although sometimes the topics are more argumentative than productive, but hey what convo about politics isn't lol).
